To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the burial diagenesis in the Lower Devonian (Lower Givetian to Upper Givetian) of the La Vid Group in Cantabrian Zone of NW Spain is characterized by: (1) a covariance of carbon- and oxygen isotope ratios with magnetic susceptibility, (2) a covariance of Sr-isotope ratios with magnetic susceptiblity, and (3) an inverse covariance of magnetic susceptibility with Fe.

the burial diagenesis in the Lower Devonian of NW Spain is characterized by the migration of a reducing petroliferous fluid, which is enriched in radiogenic 87Sr/86Sr and 13C and depleted in 18O and 34S.

(1) the magnetic susceptibility of the La Vid Group is a result of the presence of diagenetic iron-bearing carbonates; (2) these iron-bearing carbonates are the main carriers of the covariance of C- and 0-isotopes with the magnetic susceptibility; and (3) the iron-bearing carbonates were formed during the burial diagenesis as a result of upward migration of a petroliferous fluid.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

burial diagenesis, and in particular, the migration of petroliforous formation fluids, may cause a covariance or correlation of carbon and oxygen isotopes and of magnetic susceptibility, and in addition, of strontium isotopic composition.
the burial diagenesis is a major factor in controlling the isotopic and chemical composition of sandstones, dolostones, and carbonates.
the magnetic susceptibility is an excellent tool in the study of the burial diagenesis and hydrocarbon migration in sandstones and carbonic rocks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a correlation between magnetic susceptibility, carbon and oxygen isotopes, strontium isotope values, and Fe is a result of the burial diagenetic process, i.e., the formation of Fe-carbonate cements in primary voids, secondary voids, and fractures, which are the carriers for magnetic susceptibility, carbon isotope values, oxygen isotope values, strontium values, and Fe.
the magnetic susceptibility of the studied samples is a good indicator for the presence of secondary diagenetic Fe-oxides and Fe-carbonates.
the burial diagenetic processes of the La Vid Group were controlled by the migration of a reducing iron-bearing petroliferous fluid, which was depleted in 12C and 18O, and carried radiogenic 87Sr.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the covariance of magnetic susceptibility with carbon and oxygen isotopes can be used as an indicator of the burial diagenetic history of sedimentary rocks.

the burial diagenesis in the La Vid Group is a result of a complex interaction of several processes, including the migration and entrapment of petroliferous fluids, which is not reflected by the bulk-rock geochemistry.
the burial history of the La Vid Group is characterized by a progressive reduction in the amount of oxygen and carbon available for diagenetic reactions.
